what_happened: Scene layout 8 (log-cabin kitchen, robot right of the dishwasher; same view as s4), red cup_4 and wooden bowl_7. Stage 0: bowl grasped 200-208 (lift 0.099), released on the slid-out rack 390; stage 0 complete 390 (normal). Stage 1: cup grasped 510-518 (lift 0.03), carried over the rack and lowered straight into the bowl (wrist 580-632: the cup's mouth over the bowl); released 630 standing upright INSIDE the bowl (660-720), so it touches only the bowl, never the rack (at_target never true; end position 1.5 cm from the bowl centre and 4 cm higher). The placement pushed the bowl (stage 0 undone 621-622). From 760 to 1200 the gripper stayed low over the nested pair: it nudged the cup and bowl (bowl touch 818-825, 857-870; the cup tipped to ~47 deg against the bowl from 858) and closed on air at 926, 952 and 1016 near the cup, apparently trying to re-grasp it, without lifting anything. It never pushed the rack in with a closing intent or went to the door (closedness 0.00 at the end).
causal_chain: cup released at 630 directly above the bowl -> cup sits inside the bowl, not touching the rack -> stage 1 never holds -> policy hovers and pokes at the cup-in-bowl 760-1200 (three closes on air) -> neither stage 1 nor the door done at timeout
self_recovery: Possibly: three closes on air next to the cup (926, 952, 1016) look like re-grasp attempts; none touched/lifted the cup.
official_criterion_notes: Cup nested in the bowl on the top rack does not count (no rack contact); packet and video agree. dishwasher gripper_touch_intervals 755-1124 are mostly contacts with the rack wires (the rack is part of the dishwasher fixture), not door contacts. Both dishes end with dist_to_target 0.0 because the rack was shoved partly into the tub during the poking.
uncertain_about: Whether the post-placement hovering is a deliberate re-grasp attempt or a stall.
